title: Electronic Reconstruction at the Quasicrystal-Moiré Crossover in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Kuo-En Chang, Aitor Garcia-Ruiz, Ta-Lei Chou, Yen-Ting Liu, Sheng-Chin Ho, Yu-Chiang Hsieh, Ching-Hua Kao, Chiu-Hua Huang, Ying-Mei Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming-Wen Chu, Ming-Hao Liu, Tse-Ming Chen
abstract: Large twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene are widely expected to be electronically trivial, with negligible interlayer coupling and no electronic reconstruction, in contrast to the rich moiré-driven band reconstruction and correlated physics that emerge at small twist angles. Here, we show that this paradigm breaks down near a twist angle of 29°, where the system crosses over between quasicrystalline and commensurate order. Atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly reveals the coexistence of near-dodecagonal quasicrystalline symmetry and emerging moiré periodicity, indicating an intermediate, nonperiodic structural regime. Magnetotransport measurements uncover strong interlayer hybridization mediated by Umklapp scattering, manifested by magneto-intersubband oscillations and a highly unconventional Landau-level spectrum. Remarkably, the Landau-level degeneracy evolves from 4- to 12-fold with increasing temperature, a behavior incompatible with two decoupled graphene monolayers. These findings establish large-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a platform where quasiperiodic symmetry fundamentally reshapes low-energy electronic states beyond the conventional moiré framework.
summary: This work demonstrates that twisted bilayer graphene exhibits rich electronic physics near the crossover between quasicrystalline and moiré order at $	heta \approx 29^\circ$. By combining TEM and magnetotransport, the authors show that quasiperiodicity fundamentally alters low-energy states, evidenced by an anomalous, temperature-dependent evolution of the Landau-level degeneracy. This challenges existing models by proving that strong interlayer coupling persists even outside the conventional moiré regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates the electronic reconstruction in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) at a twist angle ($\approx 29^\circ$) that lies between the quasicrystalline and commensurate moiré regimes.
main_result: The conventional view that large-angle TBG is electronically trivial breaks down, as the system exhibits strong, temperature-dependent interlayer hybridization leading to an anomalous evolution of Landau-level degeneracy from fourfold to twelvefold.
method: The study combines atomic-resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to map structural symmetry with magnetotransport measurements (Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations) to probe electronic states.
model_or_system: The physical system is TBG, focusing on the crossover regime near $29^\circ$. The physics involves Umklapp scattering mediating interlayer coupling, which fundamentally reshapes the low-energy electronic states beyond standard moiré band theory.
key_observables: Landau-level degeneracy (evolving from 4-fold to 12-fold), magneto-intersubband oscillations (MISO), and the deviation from expected transport signatures at $29^\circ$.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), specifically the crossover point near $29^\circ$, and temperature ($T$) dependence.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed transport anomalies are due to the interplay between quasiperiodic symmetry and interlayer Umklapp scattering, challenging models based solely on decoupled or purely commensurate structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural transition from 12-fold quasicrystal symmetry ($30^\circ$) through the $29^\circ$ crossover state to the commensurate moiré lattice ($27.8^\circ$), alongside transport maps showing the anomalous evolution of quantum Hall plateaus.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the structural context via TEM, then uses magnetotransport measurements to probe the electronic consequences of the quasicrystal-moiré crossover, culminating in the observation of temperature-dependent Landau level degeneracy.
why_interesting: The observation of temperature-dependent, high-fold Landau level degeneracy in a quasiperiodic system provides a rich platform for studying emergent many-body physics and how geometric symmetry dictates correlated electronic behavior, relevant to understanding topological phases.
